label: Leaders on a Market Dip
about: When the whole market is short-term oversold (SPY RSI(2) low), buy the relative-strength leaders that dipped with it: strong stocks above a rising 50-day that closed below their 5-day average. The trigger is the market, not the stock, so these come in clusters on selloff days.

source.title: Market-wide oversold as the edge for buying leaders (Connors' SPY RSI(2) filter applied to stocks)

label: ETF First Pullback Through the 20-Day
about: An ETF in an uptrend that has held above its 20-day average for a week closes below it for the first time: the first pullback in a trend is the one most often bought. Buy the next session; sell on a close above the prior day's high.

source.title: First pullback to a rising moving average (classic trend-following entry)

label: Deep Stretch Below the 4-Day Mean
about: Uptrend stock or ETF closes more than 1.5 ATR below its 4-day average price: a statistically rare stretch measured in the stock's own volatility rather than by RSI. Buy the next session and target the 4-day mean.

source.title: ATR-normalised stretch from a short mean (mean-reversion literature, e.g. Quantified Strategies 'mean reversion' tests)
